sources.entry: Siliconed - Local AI image generation and instruction-based image editing on Apple silicon, with Civitai LoRAs.

summary.one_liner: Siliconed is a free, open-source macOS app that runs recent open-weight diffusion models locally on Apple silicon Macs for text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing, with Civitai and Hugging Face LoRA import.
keywords: run ai image model on mac
summary.what_it_does: Siliconed generates images from text prompts and edits existing images from a written instruction, using recent open-weight models such as Krea 2 Turbo, Z-Image Turbo, Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo, Anima Turbo and MOSS-Image (beta). It is written natively in Swift and Metal and runs without Python, a server, or the cloud, and works offline once a model is installed. Models install from inside the app, and the user chooses which ones. The app can import LoRAs and fine-tunes from Civitai or Hugging Face. It includes an explore grid of quick low-cost previews across seeds, steps, LoRA strengths or models before a full render. It can also render on another paired Mac over an encrypted connection, and a terminal tool called silicontrol drives the running app for scripts. The README states that it caps memory use to a fixed budget so large models can run on a 16 GB Mac by reading weights from disk as needed.
use_cases: generate images from text on a Mac offline
edit a photo by describing the change
explore image variations before a final render
run large diffusion models on a 16 GB Mac
use Civitai LoRAs with a local image model
render on a second Mac on the same network
how_to_run: Download the .dmg from the Releases page
Requires macOS 26 or later and Apple silicon
Install models from inside the app, choosing which ones you want
To build from source, see docs/ENGINE.md (Build from source)
stack: diffusers and transformers (used as reference implementations for checks)
notable: Runs natively in Swift and Metal with no Python, server, or cloud dependency
Memory budget capped at three quarters of Mac memory minus 2 GB, with weights streamed from disk
Checks each stage channel by channel against reference implementations in fp32
Auto-tunes kernels on the user's chip before the first render
Optional remote rendering from a MacBook to a paired Mac mini with an encrypted link
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and Apple silicon (M1 or later)
Model weights are not included; each is downloaded separately under its own license
Performance figures in the README are from specific hardware such as an M1 Pro with 16 GB
